findings.businessImpact: Conflicting declarations give search systems competing signals about which URL should represent the service page. Effects on index selection, discovery, leads and bookings remain unmeasured.
findings.description: The synthetic 11:30 UTC export marks all three layers complete. Source head declares https://atlas.example/services, rendered head declares https://atlas.example/booking, and the HTTP Link projection lists no canonical target. See inputs/page-capture.json:11-28. Both observed URLs pass the scoped format check. The conflict fails consistency, while owner intent remains unknown.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the intended target with the SEO owner. If a fresh capture reproduces the mismatch, trace which server, template or client code emits each declaration and align the declarations that are present to the approved target.
findings.title: Source and rendered canonical declarations disagree on /services
findings.verification: In a separately authorized fresh window, capture source HTML, rendered DOM and final response Link headers for the same URL, mobile profile and anonymous state. Confirm that all canonical declarations that are present agree with the owner-approved target and that the target is reachable and indexable as intended. Assess Google-selected canonical separately from a scoped URL Inspection export.

methodology: Coverage concerns declared checks, not every possible website defect.
Historical measurements are retained separately from current observations.
Structural validation and attributed review do not independently authenticate provider data.
No raw evidence payloads are included; inspect the source run using its recorded digest.
Redaction requires review; pattern matching is not a guarantee that every confidential value was identified.

narrative.text: Draft offline audit for Atlas demonstration business (atlas-demo / website), with lead-generation and booking profiles per inputs/brief.md:3-8. Full intake covers the declared dossier only. It contains one named page capture, /services on mobile in the anonymous state, plus a later failed attempt for the same scope. /booking appears only as a canonical target and has no independent capture. Zero pages are fully audited across the broader modules. URL discovery, page content and other devices and states remain unverified.

The supplied 11:30 UTC capture was 1,800 seconds old at the 2026-11-19 12:00 UTC assessment, inside the 3,600-second maximum age and the 11:00 inclusive to 12:00 exclusive UTC evidence window. Freshness applies at that assessment time. The export provides typed projections; native HTML, DOM and headers were unavailable for independent confirmation.

The separate synthetic attempt-one from collector synthetic-export-1 ran 11:35–11:36 UTC on 2026-11-19 for /services, mobile, anonymous. The export records browser-unavailable (inputs/collection-attempt.json:18) and an unknown acquisition result, with no replacement capture, authenticated execution or semantic acceptance. The earlier supplied capture remains assessable within its window. Website engineering should retain failure diagnostics and use a newly declared window for any separately authorized retry.

Production behavior, provider index state, Google-selected canonical, target status and indexability, hreflang, structured data, channel traffic, conversions and consent behavior remain unknown. Page copy, content quality, answer extractability and evidence of AI mentions or citations were unavailable. No field or lab performance data, manual accessibility results or journey evidence was supplied. The assessment has no independent reviewer decision.

Search owner should provide read-only Search Console page/query exports and Bing Webmaster search performance exports separately, with verified property/site, dates, timezone, filters, dimensions, pagination or export limits and source metadata. Provide exact /services URL Inspection separately, including the inspected property, retrieval time, last crawl, index verdict and Google-selected canonical when returned. Preserve unsupported fields and no-data states.

Analytics owner should export GA4 reports with property, dates, timezone, event and key-event definitions, filters and pagination, plus the tested GTM container version JSON and its environment. Business systems owner should provide a de-identified lead and booking status export with event timestamps, agreed stage definitions and pseudonymous join keys including failed or unmatched outcomes. Implementation owner should provide existing authorized traces that link action, dataLayer, tag, request and any provider receipt for each agreed outcome.

Website and content owners should provide a scoped URL inventory or sitemap export, original HTML and rendered captures with timestamps and response metadata, approved claim sources, audience and languages. Product owner should provide step-level lead and booking journey records with device, source, failures and funnel denominators. If AI visibility is in scope, the search owner should supply attributed response-level observations with query, surface, date, locale, response text or screenshot, and cited URLs.

Privacy policy owner should supply the approved consent matrix by region and state. Implementation owner should export sanitized default, reject, accept, selective, revoke and persistence traces. Performance owner should provide native CrUX field exports keyed by URL or origin, device and collection period, and comparable Lighthouse navigation JSON with run settings and failed samples retained. Accessibility reviewer should provide automated output with tool version and manual keyboard, focus, error-recovery and assistive-technology records for agreed journeys.
